knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 4 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other/Supervisor/Director/Treasurers and Controllers titles), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first; then a documented DreamCo manual override (authored/target_overrides.json) changed the rule output (13-1082.00, 13-1111.00, 13-1141.00) to 13-1082.00, 13-1111.00, 13-1071.00

entry_target_review.reason: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists was replaced by the broader Human Resources Specialists role, which hires generalist business graduates far more often; Project Management Specialists and Management Analysts are kept.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You are the project specialist for moving a 60-person insurance office to a new building in eight weeks. The team: facilities coordinator, IT technician, HR generalist, an office manager, two volunteer 'floor captains', and the moving vendor. Build a responsibility assignment (RACI) matrix for the twelve main work packages, explain how you matched duties to people's skills and workloads, how you will confirm each person accepts their assignments, and how you will rebalance if someone becomes overloaded.

rubric.description: Each work package has exactly one accountable owner, and responsible, consulted and informed roles are sensible.
Assignments reflect skills, authority and availability rather than convenience.
Includes a step for confirming assignments and a concrete method for detecting and fixing overload.

reference_answer_outline: Work packages: floor plan, IT network and phones, furniture, vendor contract, employee communication, packing, security badges, parking, mail forwarding, go-live support.
IT technician accountable for network cutover; HR for employee communication; facilities for vendor coordination.
Kickoff meeting where owners confirm scope and capacity.
Weekly status check of hours and task counts per person.
Rebalance by shifting tasks to floor captains or adding vendor support.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A regional hospital's outpatient clinic says patients wait too long for appointments and staff blame 'the scheduling system'. You are the management analyst assigned to find out what is really happening. Write the information-gathering plan: who you will interview and what you will ask, what data you will pull (scheduling records, no-show rates, provider templates), what you will observe in person, and how you will organize the findings (process map, issue log, data summary) so they can be analyzed next week.

rubric.description: Combines interviews, system data and direct observation and includes front-line staff and patients, not only managers.
Questions and data requests target the problem (lead time to appointment, template rules, no-shows, cancellations).
Specifies the structure for organizing information so it can be analyzed and verified.

reference_answer_outline: Interviews: schedulers, nurses, two providers, clinic manager, a handful of patients.
Data: days to third-next-available appointment, no-show and late cancel rates, template blocks by provider, call abandonment.
Observation: shadow the scheduling desk for a morning.
Organize: current-state process map, issue log tagged by cause, summary tables.
Validate findings with a short readback session with staff.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A growing regional logistics company must hire 40 warehouse associates and 6 shift supervisors in the next four months for a new distribution center, in a town with low unemployment. Write the recruiting strategy: the workforce need by role and month, target candidate sources, the employer value proposition you would promote, the selection process with time-to-hire targets, how you ensure fair and lawful hiring, and the metrics you will track weekly.

rubric.description: Ties sourcing volume to the hiring target using realistic funnel assumptions (applicants per hire).
Sources and messaging fit a tight local market (referral bonuses, community partners, shift flexibility, internal promotion for supervisors).
Includes consistent structured selection and lawful practices, plus weekly metrics such as time-to-fill and offer acceptance.

reference_answer_outline: Hiring calendar: ramp by month to match the facility opening.
Funnel: estimated applicants per hire for associates and supervisors.
Sources: job boards, workforce centers, community colleges, referral bonus, internal postings for supervisors.
Structured interviews with scored questions; consistent background-check policy.
Metrics: applicants, interviews, offers, acceptances, 90-day retention.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A city library system wants a project to add self-service laptop lending kiosks at four branches. Stakeholders include branch managers, IT, the finance office, the library board, and patrons. Plan a two-hour requirements workshop and its outputs: the agenda, techniques you will use to draw out needs and conflicts, how you will separate objectives from solutions, a draft project charter section listing objectives with success measures, and how disagreements will be resolved.

rubric.description: Agenda and techniques give all stakeholder groups a voice, including patron input gathered beforehand.
Objectives are specific and measurable (e.g. availability rate, cost per loan, damage rate), separate from solution features.
States a clear decision process for conflicting requirements, such as a priority scheme and a sponsor decision.

reference_answer_outline: Pre-work: short patron survey and branch usage data.
Agenda: purpose, current-state stories, needs brainstorming, prioritization, constraints, next steps.
Techniques: affinity grouping, MoSCoW prioritization, dot voting.
Charter: objectives with targets, scope, constraints (budget, privacy), assumptions.
Escalate unresolved conflicts to the project sponsor with options documented.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented findings from the clinic study: average wait to a new appointment is 34 days; 18 percent of booked slots are no-shows; providers each block 4 hours a week that are often unused; schedulers spend 30 percent of their time on reminder calls; and appointment types have 11 different lengths. Write the analysis and options paper: root causes supported by the data, three alternative solutions (for example, automated reminders, template simplification, overbooking rules or open-access scheduling), the expected impact and cost of each, risks, and the recommended sequence.

rubric.description: Root causes are linked to the evidence and quantified where possible (lost capacity from no-shows and unused blocks).
Options are distinct, with impact estimates, costs and risks.
Recommends a sequence with quick wins and a pilot, and how success will be measured.

reference_answer_outline: Lost capacity estimate from no-shows and unused blocked time.
Option 1: automated text reminders to cut no-shows and free scheduler time.
Option 2: simplify appointment lengths to three or four types.
Option 3: release unused blocked time 48 hours ahead; limited overbooking based on no-show prediction.
Pilot in one clinic for eight weeks, measure wait time and no-show rate.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A 200-employee company is introducing a new paid leave policy because of a new state paid sick leave law, and managers are confused about how it interacts with existing vacation days and with federal family and medical leave. Write a one-page manager brief and a ten-question employee FAQ: what the policy provides, accrual and use rules, documentation that can and cannot be requested, non-retaliation, and where to get help. Note which points you would confirm with legal counsel, and invent no specific statutory numbers without labeling them as placeholders.

rubric.description: Explains rules clearly, labels placeholders for state-specific figures, and flags items needing legal confirmation.
The manager brief focuses on what managers must do; the FAQ uses plain language employees can act on.
Covers non-retaliation, confidentiality of medical information and consistent application.

reference_answer_outline: Brief: what changes, effective date, manager duties (approve, record, never discourage use).
Accrual rate placeholder, carryover and caps, permitted uses including family care.
Documentation: limits on asking for medical details; follow the law's thresholds.
Interaction with vacation and family and medical leave explained with an example.
FAQ ends with HR contact and a confidential reporting channel.
